question.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & -6 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 25 & -25\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-4 \\ 25{x}_{3}=-25.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second   equation yields

$$
{x}_{2}+3(-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-1.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(-1)-(-1)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

So, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-1)+(-1)=-1.
$$
